meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: due on the day of discharge (employee may request payment in writing)
facts.summary: Missouri: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due due on the day of discharge (employee may request payment in writing).
facts.evidence_quote: Whenever any person, firm or corporation doing business in this state shall discharge, with or without cause, or refuse to further employ any servant or employee thereof, the unpaid wages of the servant or employee then earned at the contract rate, without abatement or deduction, shall be and become due and payable on the day of the discharge
facts.source_publisher: Revisor of Statutes, State of Missouri
facts.notes: Penalty provisions apply after the employee's written request (same section).

facts.value: No Missouri deadline when an employee quits; wages not paid by the next regular pay period can be collected by legal action
facts.summary: Missouri has no final-pay deadline for employees who quit; unpaid wages after the next regular pay period can be pursued by legal action.
facts.evidence_quote: There are no requirements under Missouri law that address when wages are due when an employee quits a job. If wages are not paid by the next regular pay period, then the wages can be collected by legal action.
facts.source_title: If an employee quits his job, when are the final wages due to him? (Missouri DOLIR)
facts.source_publisher: Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Missouri basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $15.00.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $15.00 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 2 : Weekly - 40 In addition to the exemption for federally covered employment, the law exempts, among others, employees of a retail or service business with gross annual sales or business done of less than $500,000. Premium pay required after 52 hours in seasonal amusement or recreation businesses.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Missouri does not require reporting of independent contractors (per OCSE).
facts.evidence_quote: Missouri, Independent Contractor Reporting Required?: No
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Read from the OCSE guide table (Missouri entry updated 04/23/2025). The PDF lays columns side by side; the evidence quote is the table cell read in context, not a contiguous text string.

facts.summary: Missouri: report a new hire within 20 days of the hire date.
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Employers are required to report newly hired employees within 20 calendar days of the hire date. Within 20 days of hire date.
facts.notes: RSMo 285.300. Electronic or magnetic reporters may instead use two monthly transmissions. The OCSE entry (updated 04/23/2025) also says 20 calendar days.

facts.summary: Missouri: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Semi-monthly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Missouri is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
